name: rowProds
title: Calculates the product for each row in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the product for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowProds(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE,
  method = c("direct", "expSumLog"), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows, cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows (and/or columns) to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: A character string specifying how each product is calculated. The first element is used. "direct" multiplies with prod(). "expSumLog" calls product().

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: method = "expSumLog" calls product(), which multiplies through a sum of logs and keeps the sign. method = "direct" calls base::prod(). The default is direct, because method[1] of c("direct", "expSumLog") is "direct". A prefix such as "exp" is not matched. An empty selection has product 1. With expSumLog, na.rm = FALSE, and a missing value in the row, the result is missing. A direct product of 0 and Inf is NaN. A long direct product of numbers on (0.5, 1.5) underflows to 0.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length N (K).

translation.description: Calculates the product for each row (column) in a matrix.
translation.usage:
rowProds(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, method="direct",
          dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array, or a one-dimensional vector when dim is given. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A missing double is NaN. Integer and logical matrices are accepted. expSumLog rejects a logical matrix.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. Zeros are dropped and negative values exclude, as in R. A positive index below 1 truncates to 0 and is dropped. A positive index past the margin is an error.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm. An empty product, including a row that is entirely missing when na_rm is True, is 1.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: "direct" multiplies in float64. "expSumLog" calls product() on each row. Only the first string is used, and it must match exactly. The default is direct.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the shape of x, also when x is not a matrix. This is dim. When x is one-dimensional, the values fill that shape in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility with useNames. The result is always a plain float64 vector; names are not attached.

translation.details: direct is a float64 product along the row, so a long product of uniforms on (0.5, 1.5) underflows to 0 and 0 times Inf is NaN. expSumLog imports product from matrixstats.product, which sums logs of absolute values and tracks the sign. Integer expSumLog keeps a zero positive. An empty row product is 1. A missing double is NaN.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length N, one product for each selected row.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowprods import rowProds

x = np.array([[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]], dtype=float)
rowProds(x)
